A \( 3 \times 3 \) symmetric matrix \( Q_{k} \) has eigenvalues \( \lambda_1 = 12 \), \( \lambda_2 = 3 \), and \( \lambda_3 = 14 \). Determine the trace \( \text{tr}(Q_{k}) \).
questions.answer: The trace equals \( \lambda_1 + \lambda_2 + \lambda_3 = 29 \).

questions.q: A linear transformation \( T: \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2 \) is defined by \( T(\mathbf{x}) = A\mathbf{x} \), where \( A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 \end{pmatrix} \). If \( \mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix} \), find \( T(\mathbf{v}) \).
questions.answer: To find \( T(\mathbf{v}) \), we multiply the matrix \( A \) by the vector \( \mathbf{v} \). \( T(\mathbf{v}) = A\mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix} \). Performing the matrix-vector multiplication: \( T(\mathbf{v}) = \begin{pmatrix} (2 \times 1) + (1 \times 2) \\ (1 \times 1) + (3 \times 2) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 + 2 \\ 1 + 6 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 7 \end{pmatrix} \). Thus, the correct answer is \(\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 7 \end{pmatrix}\).

questions.q: Consider the matrix \( A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 \end{pmatrix} \). If a point \( P=(x,y) \) is transformed by \( A \) to \( P'=(x',y') \), such that \( \begin{pmatrix} x' \\ y' \end{pmatrix} = A \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix} \), what is the image of the point \( (3,1) \) under this transformation?
questions.answer:
The transformation is defined by the matrix multiplication \( \begin{pmatrix} x' \\ y' \end{pmatrix} = A \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix} \). We are given the point \( (3,1) \), so \( \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} \) and the matrix \( A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 \end{pmatrix} \). Performing the matrix multiplication:

\( \begin{pmatrix} x' \\ y' \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} (2 \times 3) + (1 \times 1) \\ (1 \times 3) + (3 \times 1) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 6 + 1 \\ 3 + 3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 7 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix} \)

Therefore, the image of the point \( (3,1) \) is \( (7,6) \).

questions.q: Consider two vectors \( \mathbf{v}_1 = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} \) and \( \mathbf{v}_2 = \begin{pmatrix} -4 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} \). What is the dot product \( \mathbf{v}_1 \cdot \mathbf{v}_2 \)?
questions.answer:
\( \text{The dot product of two vectors } \mathbf{v}_1 = \begin{pmatrix} a \\ b \end{pmatrix} \text{ and } \mathbf{v}_2 = \begin{pmatrix} c \\ d \end{pmatrix} \text{ is given by } \mathbf{v}_1 \cdot \mathbf{v}_2 = ac + bd. \)

\( \text{In this case, } \mathbf{v}_1 = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} \text{ and } \mathbf{v}_2 = \begin{pmatrix} -4 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}. \)

\( \text{Therefore, } \mathbf{v}_1 \cdot \mathbf{v}_2 = (3)(-4) + (4)(3) = -12 + 12 = 0. \)

\( \text{A dot product of 0 indicates that the vectors are orthogonal.} \)

questions.q: Consider the following system of linear equations represented by the augmented matrix: \[ \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & | & 5 \\ 2 & -1 & | & 0 \end{pmatrix} \]. Use row reduction to transform the matrix into row-echelon form and determine the unique solution \( (x, y) \) for the system. What is the value of \( x \)?
questions.answer:
We are given the augmented matrix: \[ \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & | & 5 \\ 2 & -1 & | & 0 \end{pmatrix} \]
To transform this matrix into row-echelon form, we can perform the following row operation: \( R_2 \leftarrow R_2 - 2R_1 \).
\[ \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & | & 5 \\ 2 - 2(1) & -1 - 2(2) & | & 0 - 2(5) \end{pmatrix} \]
\[ \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & | & 5 \\ 0 & -5 & | & -10 \end{pmatrix} \]
Now, we can perform another row operation: \( R_2 \leftarrow R_2 / -5 \).
\[ \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & | & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & | & 2 \end{pmatrix} \]
This matrix is now in row-echelon form. The corresponding system of equations is:
\( x + 2y = 5 \)
\( y = 2 \)
Substitute the value of \( y \) into the first equation:
\( x + 2(2) = 5 \)
\( x + 4 = 5 \)
\( x = 1 \)
Therefore, the unique solution is \( (1, 2) \), and the value of \( x \) is 1.

questions.q: Consider the vector \( \mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ -12 \end{pmatrix} \). Calculate the magnitude of \( \mathbf{v} \), denoted as \( \lVert\mathbf{v}\rVert \).
questions.answer: The magnitude of a vector \( \mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix} \) in \( \mathbb{R}^2 \) is given by the formula \( \lVert\mathbf{v}\rVert = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} \). For the given vector \( \mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ -12 \end{pmatrix} \), we have \( x=5 \) and \( y=-12 \). Therefore, \( \lVert\mathbf{v}\rVert = \sqrt{(5)^2 + (-12)^2} = \sqrt{25 + 144} = \sqrt{169} = 13 \).

questions.q: Consider the vector \( \mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} \). If this vector is plotted on a standard \( xy \)-plane, it represents a directed line segment from the origin to the point \( (3,4) \). What is the geometric interpretation of the length of this vector?
choices: The vector's direction in the xy-plane.
The angle the vector makes with the positive x-axis.
The distance of the point (3,4) from the origin.
The sum of the components of the vector.
questions.answer: The length of a vector \( \mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix} \) is given by its magnitude, \( \lVert\mathbf{v}\rVert = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} \). Geometrically, this corresponds to the distance from the origin \( (0,0) \) to the point \( (x,y) \) on the Cartesian plane, as described by the Pythagorean theorem. For \( \mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} \), the length is \( \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{9 + 16} = \sqrt{25} = 5 \). This value represents the distance of the point \( (3,4) \) from the origin.

questions.q: Consider a parallelepiped in \( \mathbb{R}^3 \) formed by the origin and the three vectors \( \mathbf{u} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \ 1 \ k \end{pmatrix} \), \( \mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \ 3 \ 0 \end{pmatrix} \), and \( \mathbf{w} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \ 2 \ 4 \end{pmatrix} \). The volume of this parallelepiped is given as 24 cubic units. Find the value of \( k \) if \( k > 0 \).
questions.answer:
The volume of a parallelepiped formed by three vectors \( \mathbf{u}, \mathbf{v}, \mathbf{w} \) is given by the absolute value of their scalar triple product, which can be computed as the absolute value of the determinant of the matrix formed by these vectors as columns (or rows).

Let the matrix be \( M = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 & 0 \ 1 & 3 & 2 \ k & 0 & 4 \end{pmatrix} \).

The determinant of \( M \) is calculated as:
\( \det(M) = 2 \begin{vmatrix} 3 & 2 \ 0 & 4 \end{vmatrix} - 1 \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 \ k & 4 \end{vmatrix} + 0 \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 3 \ k & 0 \end{vmatrix} \)
\( \det(M) = 2((3)(4) - (2)(0)) - 1((1)(4) - (2)(k)) + 0 \)
\( \det(M) = 2(12) - (4 - 2k) \)
\( \det(M) = 24 - 4 + 2k \)
\( \det(M) = 20 + 2k \)

The volume of the parallelepiped is given as 24 cubic units. Therefore, \( |\det(M)| = 24 \).
\( |20 + 2k| = 24 \).

This gives two possibilities:
1. \( 20 + 2k = 24 \)
   \( 2k = 4 \)
   \( k = 2 \)

2. \( 20 + 2k = -24 \)
   \( 2k = -44 \)
   \( k = -22 \)

Since the problem states that \( k > 0 \), the correct value for \( k \) is 2.

Common Algebraic Trap: Students might forget to take the absolute value of the determinant, or they might make errors in the cofactor expansion. If \( k=-22 \) was chosen, it would be incorrect due to the condition \( k>0 \).

questions.q: A parallelogram in the xy-plane is defined by the vectors \( \mathbf{u} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} \) and \( \mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} \). What is the area of this parallelogram?
questions.answer: The area of a parallelogram defined by two vectors \( \mathbf{u} = \begin{pmatrix} u_1 \\ u_2 \end{pmatrix} \) and \( \mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} v_1 \\ v_2 \end{pmatrix} \) in \( \mathbb{R}^2 \) is given by the absolute value of the determinant of the matrix formed by these vectors as columns (or rows).  In this case, the matrix is \( A = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 4 \end{pmatrix} \). The determinant of \( A \) is \( \det(A) = (3)(4) - (1)(1) = 12 - 1 = 11 \).  Therefore, the area of the parallelogram is \( |11| = 11 \).

questions.q: A solid object in \(\mathbb{R}^3\) is defined by the region bounded by the planes \(x=0\), \(y=0\), \(z=0\), and the plane passing through the points \( P=(6,0,0) \), \( Q=(0,4,0) \), and \( R=(0,0,3) \). If a linear transformation \( T: \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3 \) is represented by the matrix \( M = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 \end{pmatrix} \), what is the volume of the transformed solid object?
questions.answer: The volume of the solid region bounded by the coordinate planes and the plane passing through \( P=(6,0,0) \), \( Q=(0,4,0) \), and \( R=(0,0,3) \) can be calculated. The equation of the plane passing through these points is given by \( \frac{x}{6} + \frac{y}{4} + \frac{z}{3} = 1 \). This is a tetrahedron with vertices at \( (0,0,0) \), \( (6,0,0) \), \( (0,4,0) \), and \( (0,0,3) \). The volume of such a tetrahedron is \( V_{original} = \frac{1}{6} |abc| \), where \( a, b, c \) are the intercepts on the axes. Thus, \( V_{original} = \frac{1}{6} |6 \cdot 4 \cdot 3| = \frac{1}{6} |72| = 12 \) cubic units. The linear transformation \( T \) is represented by the matrix \( M \). The volume of the transformed solid object is given by \( V_{transformed} = |\det(M)| \cdot V_{original} \). The determinant of \( M \) is \( \det(M) = 1 \cdot (1 \cdot 2 - 0 \cdot 0) - 0 + 0 = 2 \). Therefore, \( V_{transformed} = |2| \cdot 12 = 24 \) cubic units.

questions.q: A parallelogram in the \( xy \)-plane is defined by the vertices \( (0,0) \), \( (3,1) \), \( (1,4) \), and \( (4,5) \). What is the area of this parallelogram?
questions.answer:
The area of a parallelogram formed by vectors \( \mathbf{u} = (u_1, u_2) \) and \( \mathbf{v} = (v_1, v_2) \) originating from the same point is given by the absolute value of the determinant of the matrix formed by these vectors: \( |\det( egin{bmatrix} u_1 & v_1 \ u_2 & v_2 \end{bmatrix})| \). 

In this case, we can take the vectors originating from \( (0,0) \) to be \( \mathbf{u} = (3,1) \) and \( \mathbf{v} = (1,4) \). 

The area is \( |\det( egin{bmatrix} 3 & 1 \ 1 & 4 \end{bmatrix})| = |(3 	imes 4) - (1 	imes 1)| = |12 - 1| = |11| = 11 \).

questions.q: Consider the parallelepiped in \( \mathbb{R}^3 \) defined by the vectors \( \mathbf{u} = (2, 1, -1) \), \( \mathbf{v} = (1, k, 2) \) with \( k > 3 \), and \( \mathbf{w} = (3, 4, 1) \). If the volume of this parallelepiped is \( \frac{45}{2} \) cubic units, find the value of \( k \).
questions.answer:
The volume of the parallelepiped is the absolute value of the determinant of the matrix formed by \( \mathbf{u}, \mathbf{v}, \mathbf{w} \):
\[ \det\begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & k & 2 \\ 3 & 4 & 1 \end{pmatrix} = 2(k - 8) - 1(1 - 6) - 1(4 - 3k) = 5k - 15. \]
For \( k > 3 \), \( 5k - 15 = \frac{45}{2} \implies 5k = \frac{75}{2} \implies k = \frac{15}{2} \).

questions.q: For \( A=\left[\begin{matrix}-5 & 2\\5 & -5\end{matrix}\right] \), find entry \( (2A)_{22} \).
questions.answer: Applying Matrices & Matrix Algebra principles, \( (2A)_{22}=2(-5)=-10 \). Therefore, the verified correct option is -10.

questions.q: For \( A=\left[\begin{matrix}2 & -3\\3 & -4\end{matrix}\right] \), find entry \( (-4A)_{21} \).
questions.answer: Applying Matrices & Matrix Algebra principles, \( (-4A)_{21}=-4(3)=-12 \). Therefore, the verified correct option is -12.

questions.q: For \( A=\left[\begin{matrix}-5 & 5\\1 & 1\end{matrix}\right] \), \( B=\left[\begin{matrix}-1 & -6\\-2 & -4\end{matrix}\right] \), find entry \( (A+B)_{11} \).
questions.answer: Applying Matrices & Matrix Algebra principles, \( (A+B)_{11}=(-5)+(-1)=-6 \). Therefore, the verified correct option is -6.

questions.q: For \( A=\left[\begin{matrix}-3 & 3\\-3 & 1\end{matrix}\right] \), find entry \( (4A)_{22} \).
questions.answer: Applying Matrices & Matrix Algebra principles, \( (4A)_{22}=4(1)=4 \). Therefore, the verified correct option is 4.

questions.q: For \( A=\left[\begin{matrix}4 & 3\\6 & -3\end{matrix}\right] \), \( B=\left[\begin{matrix}5 & -6\\5 & 4\end{matrix}\right] \), find entry \( (A+B)_{11} \).
questions.answer: Applying Matrices & Matrix Algebra principles, \( (A+B)_{11}=(4)+(5)=9 \). Therefore, the verified correct option is 9.

questions.q: For \( A=\left[\begin{matrix}5 & 5\\-6 & 3\end{matrix}\right] \), \( B=\left[\begin{matrix}-4 & 5\\-5 & -5\end{matrix}\right] \), find entry \( (A+B)_{21} \).
questions.answer: Applying Matrices & Matrix Algebra principles, \( (A+B)_{21}=(-6)+(-5)=-11 \). Therefore, the verified correct option is -11.
